punchline: A man who never finished high school operated on nineteen wounded men aboard a warship, and the navy quietly asked him to leave the country.
thirty_sec: In 1951 a junk brought nineteen wounded men to HMCS Cayuga, where the only medical man, Dr. Joseph Cyr, was really Ferdinand Demara, who never finished high school. He operated for 48 hours with a textbook and a field guide. Canada celebrated him, and the navy quietly sent him away. Maria Konnikova opens with him, then turns to the people who fall for cons.
